newsitem.title: SPAIN: Analysts see weak Repsol H1 results.
newsitem.headline: Analysts see weak Repsol H1 results.

text.p: Spain's Repsol is expected to have seen a lacklustre first half, with weak chemicals and gas division results seen weighing on the energy group's overall performance, analysts said on Tuesday.

Analysts forecast net attributable profit in the first half declining between two and nine percent. Operating margin will have risen at the most around 10 percent, they said. Results are provisionally set for release on Wednesday.
In the first half of 1996, Repsol posted net attributable profit of 61.45 billion pesetas ($390.4 million), with operating profit at 96.05 billion pesetas.

"The results look like they're going to be pretty lousy really, with the upstream (exploration and production) looking bad versus quarter one and the (liquid petroleum gas) price still frozen," said one oils analyst.
The price cap was removed in early August.
He said chemical results would not be outstanding after maintenance problems and partial shut-downs.
"They've been trying to filter down the idea (to analysts) that the second quarter hasn't been brilliant," he added.
A Banesto Bolsa analyst said first half operating margin will compare favourably with a poor result this time last year.

"The operating result will be good above all because the first half of 1996 was weak. Also you've got good effects like the impact of the Astra buy on refining and marketing, and the chemicals division should be helped by the recovery in base and derived prices recovering," he said.
It may only be in the second half of the year that the firm recovers some of its old verve.
Javier Borrachero, energy analyst at Central Hispano Bolsa, saw improvement later this year.
"The third and fourth quarter should see something of a pick-up (overall) helped by better chemical results, an improvement in production and the removal of the LPG price freeze," he said.

The removal of the price freeze is effective as of August 2, Repsol said on Tuesday. This should boost Repsol's fourth and first quarter results, when butane consumption usually climbs because of cold weather.

As regards the shares, analyst opinion was divided. Some saw worries over hefty investment in Latin America continuing to weigh for the short term, while others thought the shares may well rebound once first half results are out of the way.
"The oil and gas sector has underperformed for some time in Spain, unlike in the rest of Europe," said Susan Scott, energy analyst at Credit Lyonnais Securities in London.
Repsol has not taken part in a generalised outperformance by European oil companies which have benefitted from higher oil prices and a higher dollar, she explained.

"Spain isn't geared to upstream and maybe that's part of it but perhaps if investors are looking to take profits elsewhere (in the European oil sector), Repsol could see the benefit (of switching). I think there's scope for surprises on the upside or at least better indications (in the second half)," she said.
Worries over Repsol's increasing incursions in the new world, have perhaps been overdone.

"The group are starting to think about giving presentations again after the summer, and perhaps the message they want to give is that they're more focused as regards Latin America than people have given them credit for," CLS's Scott added.
Others were more cautious short term.

Banesto's target price for the shares is 6,600 pesetas, versus around 6,210 pesetas at 1400 GMT today. But this level may not be reached until the effects of investment in Latin American has disappeared, the analyst said.
"The share price hasn't taken off yet and we're not seeing the growth rates at Repsol that we've been accustomed to. But medium term I'd be a buyer," the Banesto analyst said.
-- Madrid newsroom +341 585 2160
($ = 157.4 Spanish Pesetas)
